answer: In a decentralized AI consensus network, the "Weighted Randomized Byzantine Fault Tolerance" mechanism can effectively resist fake-identity attacks. This mechanism operates by introducing a "harbor" of trusted nodes, which serve as a "wharf" for new agents to prove their identity. As new agents attempt to join, they are randomly assigned a weight, and only those with sufficient weight can participate in consensus. This forces attackers to spread their resources across multiple nebulae of fake identities, rendering their Sybil attacks less effective.
